trust_decision.summary: Whether a field resolver may run is decided by the permission's `has_permission` return value: `PermissionExtension.resolve` truth-tests the raw result on the synchronous path, so a plain `def has_permission` that returns an awaitable is always truthy and access is granted; the async path awaits the same value through `await_maybe`. Which path a field takes is fixed once at schema build by `supports_sync`, which only detects `async def` via `iscoroutinefunction`.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the synchronous permission path, and this single truthiness test is the only place a permission result is evaluated without awaiting it.

fix_sites.entry_point: any field built with permission_classes=[...] (strawberry.field, strawberry.mutation, strawberry.federation.field, strawberry.relay.connection) or with extensions=[PermissionExtension(...)], on a synchronous resolver
same PermissionExtension.resolve path; the new error surfaces to the client as a GraphQL error instead of granting the field

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Awaitable-returning permissions are legitimate on the asynchronous path: `resolve_async` awaits them via `await_maybe`, and a sync resolver with an `async def` permission is deliberately routed through `SyncToAsyncExtension`. Outside the repo the docs also promise that any truthy return grants access. An over-broad fix that rejects every awaitable (for example also inside `resolve_async`, or that requires the result to be `True`/a bool) breaks documented async permissions and truthy non-bool returns.

O6_input_shapes: plain `def has_permission` returning a coroutine object (the reported case)
plain `def` returning any non-coroutine awaitable (Future or custom `__await__`), caught by inspect.isawaitable
multiple permission instances in one PermissionExtension where any one returns an awaitable (the loop short-circuits)
unchanged: `async def has_permission` on the async path, awaited by resolve_async / await_maybe

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a node-level authorization check inside NodeExtension.resolve for node(id:) lookups, truth-testing a possibly-async permission result
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: NodeExtension is already a FieldExtension with the same paired sync/async resolve shape as PermissionExtension and wraps relay node resolution; a maintainer protecting global-ID node access would naturally add the check there and repeat the sync-path mistake.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-mutation permission gate run by InputMutationExtension before the resolver
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The extension already rewrites the resolver arguments and runs ahead of the resolver, so a mutation-level permission feature plausibly lands here and needs its own sync path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a default/merged permission applied while pydantic fields are rebuilt from an existing Strawberry field
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This merge route already copies permission_classes from the existing field, so a maintainer adding a default permission or a second check at field rebuild time would write it here, away from PermissionExtension.resolve.

O9_family: incorrect authorization / permission bypass (CWE-863); no resource-exhaustion angle
